title: Module sheaves over arbitrary ring sheaves are Grothendieck
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in a universe $\mathcal U$, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings with values in $\mathcal U$, without a commutativity assumption. The category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of left $\mathcal O$-modules with values in $\mathcal U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it is abelian, has all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, has exact $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimits, and has a generator $G$, meaning that for distinct parallel maps $f,g:M\to N$ some $h:G\to M$ satisfies $f\circ h\ne g\circ h$.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), final sentence, with the axioms of Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions). proof.text: Work directly on the given site, in the common universe w = max(c,h,r,s). Abelian sheafification and its locally bijective characterization are transported from the small model by the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances. Mathlib gives abelianness and colimits of module sheaves. The proved preservesColimitsOfShape_toSheaf instance, preservation of finite limits and reflection of isomorphisms transfer exact filtered colimits from abelian sheaves by HasExactColimitsOfShape.domain_of_functor. This is the first two local instances in the Lean proof.

For each object A construct the module presheaf L_A whose value at X is the finitely supported functions from ULift(Hom(X,A)) to R(X). A restriction along f sends the basis vector at a with coefficient b to the basis vector at f followed by a with coefficient R(f)(b). The private freeObj construction proves the functor laws on basis vectors using Finsupp.lhom_ext′ and linearCombination_single. For every section x of M over A, freeDesc sends the basis vector a to M(a)(x). Its naturality follows from the presheaf composition law; freeDesc_single computes its value, in particular giving x on the identity basis vector. This construction keeps the rings in their original universe and works for noncommutative rings.

Sheafify each L_A using the existing module sheafification adjunction. Suppose f,g:M to N agree after every map from each sheafified L_A. For any section x of M over A apply this equality to the adjoint of freeDesc(x); naturality of the adjunction gives equality after the underlying free-presheaf map. Evaluating at the identity basis vector gives f_A(x)=g_A(x). Extensionality and faithfulness of forgetting modules and restricting scalars give f=g. Thus the sheafified L_A form a separating family. Their coproduct exists since the object type of the site is small in w; ObjectProperty.IsSeparating.isSeparator_coproduct gives a separator. Together with the exact filtered colimits above this constructs IsGrothendieckAbelian. For an empty site separation is vacuous and the coproduct is the zero object.

reviewed_lean.note: The statement matches the node clause by clause. The isomorphism clause is IsIso of the derived-functor unit at the class of an arbitrary unbounded K, i.e. the specified map. The vanishing clause covers every F and q>0 via the homology of RE(F[0]). There is no commutativity, boundedness or universe-equality assumption, and the site keeps universes t+1/t. The §1(B) repair of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck is justified: the old upstream theorem needs one universe for site, ring and modules. The new isGrothendieckAbelianOfUniverses is the node's statement in a common universe, and the existing general variant needs commutative rings. Both helpers are real and sorry-free. Only the two expected node files differ, and both lean.statement strings appear verbatim. Both files compiled with no diagnostics via nt_compile.py on the side overlay. Minor, no action: the resolution helper also uses lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective, which is only in proof_deps; the statement does not depend on that proof.

lean.statement: theorem isGrothendieckAbelianOfUniverses {C : Type c} [Category.{h} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{r}) : IsGrothendieckAbelian.{max c h r s} (ringedSiteModules.{max c h r s} R)
lean.note: The recorded upstream theorem requires C : Type u with SmallCategory C and R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}, so it cannot be applied to the pro-etale site with object universe t+1, morphism universe t and independent ring universe u. This equivalent small-site interface uses the common module universe max c h r s. Existing small-model sheafification transport supplies the abelian structure without additional hypotheses. It states the same Grothendieck property for arbitrary (possibly noncommutative) ring sheaves. No site or coefficient universes are equated.
